t: Ancient writers give the Persian army as up to a million men, figures modern historians call absurd or of no use; modern estimates run from about 91,000 to 120,000.
The site of the battle is not known with certainty, and the date of 1 October 331 BCE is a calculation from an eclipse reported by ancient sources.
After the battle Darius fled east and was killed by his own satrap Bessus, and the Achaemenid Empire is traditionally considered to have ended with his death.
dyk: Darius III offered Alexander all territory west of the Euphrates, his daughter in marriage and 30,000 talents of silver before the battle, according to Diodorus, Curtius and Justin; Alexander refused.
ev: Darius III loses the Battle of Issus to Alexander, who captures his wife, mother and two daughters
Alexander takes Tyre after a siege from January to July and then Gaza, and Egypt surrenders to him
Darius makes a third offer of terms, which Alexander refuses
Alexander marches from Egypt through Syria, crosses the Euphrates and then the Tigris
The armies meet at Gaugamela and Alexander leads a wedge into the Persian centre
Darius flees and Babylon is surrendered to Alexander

f.date: 1 October 331 BCE, by calculation from the lunar eclipse of 20 to 21 September of that year
f.place: Gaugamela, a village on the river Bumodus north of Arbela (modern Erbil) in the Nineveh Plains of Iraq; the exact site is not known, and Karamlesh is the most commonly accepted
f.sides: Alexander of Macedon with Greek allies and mercenaries (Arrian gives 7,000 cavalry and 40,000 infantry, figures modern scholars generally accept) against Darius III of Persia, whose army ancient sources put at up to 1,000,000 and modern estimates at about 91,000 to 120,000, with no agreed figure
f.outcome: Darius fled the field and the Persian army broke up; Alexander took Babylon and Darius was later murdered by Bessus, ending the Achaemenid Empire.
